metadata.course: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure
metadata.attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
metadata.scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
metadata.description: The firm-and-market view: scarcity and marginal analysis, supply and demand with elasticity, production and cost, market structure from perfect competition to oligopoly, factor markets, and market failure.

id_namespace.reason: Concept ids are global; the prefix keeps this course disjoint from the shipped courses that share concept titles.

order.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
Market Failure and the Role of Government

concepts.title: Accounting profit versus economic profit
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: Economic profit subtracts implicit cost as well, so a firm can be accounting-profitable and economically breaking even.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Antitrust policy and regulation
concepts.strand: Market Failure and the Role of Government
concepts.summary: Competition policy targets market power, while regulation can address natural monopoly directly.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Asymmetric information
concepts.strand: Market Failure and the Role of Government
concepts.summary: When one side knows more, adverse selection and moral hazard can drive good participants out of the market.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Budget constraints and trade-offs
concepts.summary: A budget line shows the affordable combinations, and its slope is the relative price.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Capital markets and the rental price of capital
concepts.summary: Firms hire capital until its marginal revenue product equals the rental price.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Coase theorem and property rights
concepts.strand: Market Failure and the Role of Government
concepts.summary: With clear property rights and low bargaining cost, private parties can reach the efficient outcome themselves.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Collusion and cartels
concepts.summary: Firms can raise joint profit by acting as a monopolist, but each has an incentive to cheat.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Common resources and the tragedy of the commons
concepts.strand: Market Failure and the Role of Government
concepts.summary: Rival but non-excludable resources are overused because no one bears the full cost of their own use.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Comparative advantage and gains from trade
concepts.summary: Specialising where opportunity cost is lowest raises total output, so trade can benefit both sides.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Competitive labour market equilibrium
concepts.summary: In a competitive market the wage equals marginal revenue product for every worker hired.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Consumer and producer surplus
concepts.summary: Surplus measures the gain from trade for buyers and sellers separately.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Corrective taxes and subsidies
concepts.strand: Market Failure and the Role of Government
concepts.summary: A tax equal to the external cost, or a subsidy equal to the external benefit, realigns private with social incentives.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Deadweight loss of taxation
concepts.summary: A tax drives a wedge between price paid and price received, so some mutually beneficial trades do not happen.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Derived demand for labour
concepts.summary: Demand for a factor exists only because the factor helps produce a good that is itself demanded.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Determinants of price elasticity of demand
concepts.summary: Substitutes, share of budget, necessity and time horizon decide how responsive demand is.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Elasticity and total revenue
concepts.summary: Total revenue rises with price only when demand is inelastic, which is the practical use of the measure.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Explicit and implicit costs
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: Economic cost includes the opportunity cost of resources the owner already supplies.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Game theory and Nash equilibrium
concepts.summary: A Nash equilibrium is a set of strategies where no player can gain by changing alone.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Income and cross-price elasticity
concepts.summary: Income elasticity classifies normal and inferior goods, and cross-price elasticity identifies substitutes and complements.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Income inequality and redistribution
concepts.strand: Market Failure and the Role of Government
concepts.summary: Tax-and-transfer policy can change the distribution of income, with efficiency costs of its own.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: International trade and tariffs
concepts.summary: Opening trade raises total surplus while a tariff lowers it, though it redistributes toward domestic producers.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Least-cost combination of inputs
concepts.summary: Cost is minimised where the marginal product per dollar is equal across inputs.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Long-run average total cost and economies of scale
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: All inputs vary in the long run, so the planning curve shows economies, constant returns and diseconomies of scale.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Long-run equilibrium and normal profit
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: Free entry drives economic profit to zero, leaving firms earning only a normal profit.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Marginal analysis and decision rules
concepts.summary: A rational decision compares the marginal benefit of one more unit with its marginal cost.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Marginal revenue product
concepts.summary: A firm hires until the marginal revenue product of the factor equals its price.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Marginal social cost and marginal social benefit
concepts.strand: Market Failure and the Role of Government
concepts.summary: Social cost and benefit add the external effect to the private one, which is where the efficient quantity sits.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Marginal utility per dollar and consumer choice
concepts.summary: A consumer maximises utility by equalising marginal utility per dollar across all goods.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Market efficiency and total surplus
concepts.summary: Total surplus is maximised at competitive equilibrium, which is the efficiency benchmark for every later comparison.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Monopolistic competition
concepts.summary: Many firms sell differentiated products, so each faces a downward-sloping demand curve but no barrier to entry.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Monopolistic competition in the long run
concepts.summary: Entry erodes profit until price equals average total cost, leaving excess capacity.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Monopoly inefficiency and deadweight loss
concepts.summary: Restricting output below the competitive level leaves some mutually beneficial trades unmade.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Monopoly profit maximisation
concepts.summary: A monopolist sets output where marginal revenue equals marginal cost and prices off the demand curve.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Monopoly: sources of market power
concepts.summary: Barriers to entry such as control of a resource, patents, or scale keep rivals out and create a price maker.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Monopsony
concepts.summary: A single buyer of labour hires less and pays less than a competitive market would.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Natural monopoly and regulation
concepts.summary: When scale makes one firm cheapest, regulation targets the price rather than the number of firms.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Oligopoly and interdependence
concepts.summary: A few large firms must anticipate each other, so decisions are strategic rather than independent.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Perfect competition: characteristics
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: Many small firms, a homogeneous product and free entry make each firm a price taker.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Positive and negative externalities
concepts.strand: Market Failure and the Role of Government
concepts.summary: An externality is a cost or benefit that falls on a third party outside the transaction.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Present value and investment decisions
concepts.summary: A project is worth funding when the present value of its returns exceeds its cost.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Price ceilings and floors
concepts.summary: A binding ceiling creates a shortage and a binding floor a surplus, with deadweight loss in both cases.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Price discrimination
concepts.summary: Charging different prices to different buyers raises profit when groups can be separated and resale is blocked.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Price elasticity of demand
concepts.summary: Elasticity measures the percentage change in quantity demanded for a one per cent change in price.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Price elasticity of supply
concepts.summary: Supply elasticity depends on how quickly producers can change output, so it is larger in the long run.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Production possibilities curve
concepts.summary: The frontier shows the maximum output combinations and the opportunity cost of moving along it.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Productive and allocative efficiency
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: Perfect competition is both productively and allocatively efficient in long-run equilibrium.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Profit maximisation where marginal revenue equals marginal cost
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: Every firm maximises profit by producing where marginal revenue equals marginal cost.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Public goods and the free-rider problem
concepts.strand: Market Failure and the Role of Government
concepts.summary: Non-rival and non-excludable goods are underprovided because each user can free ride.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost
concepts.summary: Every choice costs the next-best alternative forgone, which is the source of all trade-offs.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Short-run cost curves
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: Marginal cost crosses average variable and average total cost at their minimum points.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Short-run equilibrium in perfect competition
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: Price equals marginal revenue for a price taker, so the firm produces where price equals marginal cost.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Short-run production and diminishing returns
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: With one input fixed, the marginal product of the variable input eventually falls.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Shutdown and exit decisions
concepts.strand: Production, Cost, and the Perfect Competition Model
concepts.summary: A firm shuts down in the short run when price falls below average variable cost, and exits when it falls below average total cost.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Subsidies
concepts.summary: A subsidy lowers the price buyers pay and raises the price sellers receive, at a cost to the government.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Taxes and tax incidence
concepts.summary: The statutory payer is not the economic bearer: incidence follows the relative elasticities.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Unions and bilateral bargaining
concepts.summary: Collective bargaining raises wages through higher demand or restricted supply, with employment effects.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure

concepts.title: Utility and marginal utility
concepts.summary: Total utility rises with consumption while marginal utility generally falls.

provenance.source: AP Microeconomics - Markets, Firms and Market Failure
